name: pH-Metric Titration
teachingNotes: pH-metric titration monitors electrometric pH as a function of delivered titrant volume. The inflection point on the sigmoidal titration curve identifies the exact stoichiometric equivalence point without relying on visual indicator color transitions.

steps.prompt: Step 1: Setup & calibration. Calibrate the pH meter with standard buffers and lower electrode into beaker.
steps.hint: Immerse the combination glass electrode into analyte on the magnetic stirrer, ensuring the stir bar rotates freely.
steps.completionText: pH meter calibrated; glass electrode safely positioned in analyte beaker above rotating stir bar.

steps.prompt: Step 2: Initial measurement. Record initial analyte pH before adding any titrant (V = 0.00 mL).
steps.hint: Check the digital pH meter readout with continuous magnetic stirring. Initial pH point is plotted on the live curve.
steps.completionText: Initial baseline reading recorded (V = 0.00 mL, illustrative pH = 2.80). Live graph initialized.

steps.prompt: Step 3: Titrate buffer region. Add titrant in 1.0–2.0 mL portions and plot data points on the live graph.
steps.hint: In the flat buffer region, pH changes gradually. Add 1.0–2.0 mL increments and record the reading after each addition.
steps.completionText: Titrant delivered through buffer zone; steady gradual pH rise plotted on sigmoidal curve.

steps.prompt: Step 4: Steep inflection zone! Near the equivalence point, deliver titrant dropwise in 0.1–0.2 mL portions.
steps.hint: pH changes sharply near the equivalence point (pH 4 to 10). Add very small increments (0.1–0.2 mL) to locate the inflection point accurately!
steps.completionText: Dropwise additions recorded across the steep inflection region. S-curve inflection point captured!

steps.prompt: Step 5: Identify equivalence point. Click on the steepest inflection point on the titration curve graph.
steps.hint: The equivalence point corresponds to the maximum first derivative (dpH/dV) on the sigmoidal curve.
steps.completionText: Equivalence point identified at V_eq = 22.40 mL (illustrative pH = 8.40). Potentiometric analysis complete!

coarse_steep_addition.message: Analytical flaw: Delivered a large 2.0–5.0 mL jump directly across the steep inflection region! In pH-metric titration, large increments obscure the inflection point, making accurate determination of the equivalence volume impossible.

stirrer_electrode_impact.message: Equipment hazard: Lowering the glass electrode too far into the beaker causes the spinning magnetic stir bar to collide with the fragile glass bulb, risking breakage. Always maintain at least 5 mm clearance.

unrinsed_electrode.message: Contamination: Inserting unrinsed electrode into analyte introduces foreign ions and disturbs the ionic strength of the solution.
